<reason>PRO established marginal contribution under near-zero vacancy and answered causation, funding, and trigger objections with sequencing, an external measurable test, and the distinction between freezing growth and eliminating existing fees. CON's secured-bed precondition conceded that recruitment cannot remain unconstrained, while its purpose-built housing claim never answered PRO's overflow-into-shared-housing mechanism.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: purpose-built beds absorb students only until they run out, after which overflow competes for local homes, turning CON's segregation claim into evidence for a cap.</best_rebuttal>
